name: Plainclause Custom Order Status for WooCommerce
author: plainclause

sections.description:
WooCommerce gives you seven order statuses. Real shops need more: “Awaiting stock”, “In production”, “Shipped”, “Ready for pickup”, “Quote sent”. This plugin lets you add your own order statuses and use them exactly like the built-in ones.

Add a status in a minute under WooCommerce > Order statuses: give it a name and a colour, choose whether it counts as paid, and choose who gets an email when an order reaches it. The status then appears everywhere: the Orders screen (with its colour), the status menu on each order, bulk actions, filters and the customer’s My account page.

Why this one

  • Behaves like a built-in status. Mark a status as paid (counts in reports and allows downloads) or editable (items and prices can still change).
  • Emails done the WooCommerce way. Each status can email the customer, the shop or both, using WooCommerce’s own email templates, editable under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails.
  • Safe deletes. Deleting a status first moves its orders to a status you choose, so no order goes missing.
  • Both order storage modes. Tested with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and the classic posts storage.
  • Lightweight and private. No external services, no tracking, no nag screens.

Features

  • Unlimited custom order statuses with a name, slug and colour.
  • Coloured status badges on the Orders screen.
  • “Change status to …” bulk actions (optional per status).
  • Filter the Orders screen by your statuses; order counts per status.
  • Optional email to the customer and/or the shop when an order gets a status.
  • Paid and editable options per status.
  • Default status per payment method (for example bank transfer orders go to “Awaiting payment check”).
  • Customers see the status name in My account.
  • Deleting a status moves its orders to another status.
  • Works with HPOS, the classic order storage and the cart and checkout blocks.

Pro add-on (optional)

Everything above is free and stays free. A separate paid add-on adds:

  • Automatic status changes: “after 3 days in Shipped, change to Completed”.
  • An email to the shop when an order stays in a status too long.
  • Reduce or restore stock when an order enters a status.
  • Let customers cancel their own orders in chosen statuses from My account.
  • Rename WooCommerce’s built-in statuses (for example “Processing” to “Being packed”).

Black Friday / Cyber Monday: 50% off your first payment until 1 December 2026 with the code BFCM50 (yearly, lifetime).

Plainclause Custom Order Status Pro costs from $29 a year for one site, or $79 once for a lifetime licence, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. It is sold by Freemius, our reseller and merchant of record.

More from Plainclause

  • Plainclause Sequential Order Numbers for WooCommerce: clean, gap-free order numbers with your own prefix.
  • Plainclause Store Vacation & Holiday Mode for WooCommerce: pause orders while you are away and reopen on schedule.
  • Plainclause EU Withdrawal Button & Legal Guarantee Notice: the withdrawal function and legal guarantee notice EU shops need.

For developers

  • Statuses are registered as wc-<slug> post statuses and added through wc_order_statuses, so $order->update_status( 'your-slug' ) and the woocommerce_order_status_your-slug action work as usual.
  • Actions: pccos_status_saved, pccos_status_deleted.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (WooCommerce must be active).
  2. Go to WooCommerce > Order statuses.
  3. Add a status: name, colour, paid or editable, and emails. Save.
  4. Optional: choose a default status per payment method on the same page.
sections.faq:
Where do my custom statuses appear?

On the Orders screen (with their colour and as filters), in the status menu on each order, in bulk actions, in the order preview and on the customer’s My account page.

Can I send an email when an order gets my status?

Yes. Choose “Email the customer”, “Email the shop” or both. The emails use WooCommerce’s templates and can be edited under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails.

Does a custom status count as paid?

Only if you tick “Paid”. Paid statuses count as paid orders, which allows downloads and includes them in reports.

What happens to orders when I delete a status?

You choose a status they move to (for example On hold) before the status is removed. Each order gets a note.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

Orders keep their status in the database, but WooCommerce no longer knows it, so they do not show in the order lists. Reactivate the plugin and they come back. Move orders to a built-in status first if you remove the plugin for good.

Does it work with HPOS?

Yes. It works with High-Performance Order Storage and with the classic order storage.

Does it change stock?

No. Custom statuses do not change stock in the free plugin. The Pro add-on can reduce or restore stock per status.
